historical_record.description: The Empire Malt House of John Bauer and Joseph Schweitzer, re-equipped in 1906 by the Galland-Henning Pneumatic Malting Drum Company of Milwaukee and then nearly destroyed in the earthquake and fire, was rebuilt in reinforced concrete by 1908, on a block brewers and maltsters had worked since the Lyon Brewery of 1867. It became the last malt house in North Beach and the last barrel malting plant west of the Mississippi.
Bauer & Schweitzer, which malted for Anchor Brewing and other Bay Area brewers until the 1960s, stopped supplying grain from the malt house.
Designated San Francisco Landmark No. 129, Bauer & Schweitzer Malting Company.

The Landmarks Preservation Advisory Board put forward the two malting towers and the Chestnut Street buildings for landmark status. The Planning Commission designated only the towers in March 1981, the Board of Supervisors sustained that, and the Mayor approved it on 5 June 1981.
Recorded in the city's 1982 survey of North Beach, adopted by the Board of Supervisors in 1999, as an individually listed resource. San Francisco City Landmark No. 129.

The City Planning Commission approved with conditions, 5-0, a three-year extension — not the five asked for — of the deadline to begin renovating the existing building for 122 condominium units under Motion 13021, requiring the sponsor to keep the site secure and clean (Motion 13870).
The malt house was converted into residences, with the circa-1930 brewing murals by William du Pont rehung in two lobbies.
